stem: An associate asks Claude to summarize a new regulation, and Claude produces a confident summary citing a specific subsection number. Before sending the summary to the compliance team, what is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Send it as-is, since Claude expressed high confidence.
options.why: Self-reported confidence is not a reliable accuracy signal; language models can fabricate specific-looking details such as citation numbers while sounding certain.

options.text: Verify the cited subsection against the official regulation text before sharing.
options.why: Validating factual claims, especially citations bound for a compliance audience, against an authoritative source is the diligence step required.

options.text: Ask Claude to rate its own confidence and send it if the rating is high.
options.why: A confidence rating from the model is still self-reported and does not check the citation against the real regulation.

options.text: Reword the summary to sound more formal, then send it.
options.why: Reformatting changes the tone but does nothing to address whether the cited subsection is correct.

explanation: Language models can fabricate specific-looking details such as citation numbers, a hallucination. Validating factual claims, especially citations bound for a compliance audience, against an authoritative source is the diligence step required. Self-reported confidence is not a reliable accuracy signal, and reformatting does not address correctness.
reference: CCAO-F Exam Guide v1.0 — Sample 1 (Domain 2, Output Evaluation and Validation)

stem: An associate needs to generate a high volume of short customer-reply drafts where speed and cost matter more than deep reasoning. Which choice best fits the task?

options.text: Use the most capable, highest-cost model for every reply to maximize quality.
options.why: Always using the top model wastes the cost and latency budget on straightforward work that does not need deep reasoning.

options.text: Use a faster, lower-cost model suited to straightforward, high-volume tasks.
options.why: Aligning model selection with task requirements means matching a faster, lower-cost model to straightforward, high-volume work, reserving the most capable model for complex reasoning.

options.text: Disable all product features to reduce cost.
options.why: Turning off features does not address the speed-versus-quality trade-off in model selection and may remove capabilities the task needs.

options.text: Switch to a different AI platform.
options.why: Changing platforms does not address the trade-off; the question is which Claude model fits the task's speed and cost requirements.

explanation: Aligning model selection with task requirements means matching a faster, lower-cost model to straightforward, high-volume work, reserving the most capable model for complex reasoning. Always using the top model wastes the cost and latency budget; disabling features or switching platforms does not address the trade-off.
reference: CCAO-F Exam Guide v1.0 — Sample 2 (Domain 3, Product and Model Selection)

stem: A project manager wants to upload a spreadsheet containing customer names and account numbers so Claude can analyze trends. Organizational policy restricts sharing regulated personal data. What is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Upload the file as-is, since the analysis is internal.
options.why: Uploading regulated personal identifiers as-is violates the organizational policy regardless of the analysis being internal.

options.text: Remove or anonymize the personal identifiers before uploading, consistent with policy.
options.why: Applying data-sensitivity and privacy safeguards means redacting or anonymizing regulated identifiers before use, so the analysis can proceed without exposing protected data.

options.text: Upload the file but instruct Claude not to retain it.
options.why: Instructing the model not to retain data does not satisfy the policy control; the regulated data has still been shared.
Abandoning the task is unnecessary when anonymization enables it to proceed within policy.

explanation: Applying data-sensitivity and privacy safeguards means redacting or anonymizing regulated identifiers before use, so the analysis can proceed without exposing protected data. Uploading as-is violates policy; instructing the model not to retain data does not satisfy the policy control; abandoning the task is unnecessary when anonymization enables it.
reference: CCAO-F Exam Guide v1.0 — Sample 3 (Domain 6, Governance, Risk, and Responsible Use)
